title: Hard problem
statementMd:
Vasiliy is fond of solving different tasks. Today he found one he wasn't able to solve himself, so he asks you to help.

Vasiliy is given $*n*$ strings consisting of lowercase English letters. He wants them to be sorted in lexicographical order (as in the dictionary), but he is not allowed to swap any of them. The only operation he is allowed to do is to reverse any of them (first character becomes last, second becomes one before last and so on).

To reverse the $*i*$-th string Vasiliy has to spent $*c*_{*i*}$ units of energy. He is interested in the minimum amount of energy he has to spent in order to have strings sorted in lexicographical order.

String $*A*$ is lexicographically smaller than string $*B*$ if it is shorter than $*B*$ ($|*A*| < |*B*|$) and is its prefix, or if none of them is a prefix of the other and at the first position where they differ character in $*A*$ is smaller than the character in $*B*$.

For the purpose of this problem, two equal strings nearby do not break the condition of sequence being sorted lexicographically.

## Input

The first line of the input contains a single integer $*n*$ ($2 ≤ *n* ≤ 100 000$) — the number of strings.

The second line contains $*n*$ integers $*c*_{*i*}$ ($0 ≤ *c*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$), the $*i*$-th of them is equal to the amount of energy Vasiliy has to spent in order to reverse the $*i*$-th string.

Then follow $*n*$ lines, each containing a string consisting of lowercase English letters. The total length of these strings doesn't exceed $100 000$.

## Output

If it is impossible to reverse some of the strings such that they will be located in lexicographical order, print $- 1$. Otherwise, print the minimum total amount of energy Vasiliy has to spent.

## Note

In the second sample one has to reverse string $2$ or string $3$. To amount of energy required to reverse the string $3$ is smaller.

In the third sample, both strings do not change after reverse and they go in the wrong order, so the answer is $- 1$.

In the fourth sample, both strings consists of characters '`a`' only, but in the sorted order string "`aa`" should go before string "`aaa`", thus the answer is $- 1$.
statementZhMd:
Vasiliy 喜欢解决各种各样的任务。今天，他遇到了一个自己无法解决的问题，因此请求你的帮助。

Vasiliy 有 $*n*$ 个由小写英文字母组成的字符串。他希望将这些字符串按字典序排序，但不允许交换它们。唯一可以进行的操作是将任意一个字符串反转（第一个字符变成最后一个，第二个字符变成倒数第二个，依此类推）。

反转第 $*i*$ 个字符串需要花费 $*c*_{*i*}$ 单位的能量。Vasiliy 想知道，为了使这些字符串按字典序排列，他至少需要花费多少能量。

如果字符串 $*A*$ 比字符串 $*B*$ 的字典序小，那么要么 $*A*$ 比 $*B*$ 短（$|*A*| < |*B*|$）且 $*A*$ 是 $*B*$ 的前缀；要么二者互不为对方的前缀，并且在它们首次出现不同字符的位置，$*A*$ 中的字符小于 $*B*$ 中的字符。

在本题中，相邻的两个相等字符串不会破坏序列按字典序排列的条件。

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含一个整数 $*n*$（$2 ≤ *n* ≤ 100 000$），表示字符串的数量。

第二行包含 $*n*$ 个整数 $*c*_{*i*}$（$0 ≤ *c*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$），其中第 $*i*$ 个数表示 Vasiliy 反转第 $*i*$ 个字符串所需花费的能量。

接下来 $*n*$ 行，每行包含一个由小写英文字母组成的字符串。这些字符串的总长度不超过 $100 000$。

## 输出格式

如果无法通过反转某些字符串使它们按字典序排列，输出 $- 1$。否则，输出 Vasiliy 需要花费的最小总能量。

## 说明

在第二个样例中，需要反转字符串 $2$ 或字符串 $3$。反转字符串 $3$ 所需的能量更少。

在第三个样例中，两个字符串反转后都不会改变，但它们的顺序错误，因此答案为 $- 1$。

在第四个样例中，两个字符串都只由字符 '`a`' 组成，但在排序后的顺序中，字符串 "`aa`" 应该排在字符串 "`aaa`" 之前，因此答案为 $- 1$。
